text:
Ellen: Hey team, stayed at an EU hotel for client meetings. Checkout bill shows room + VAT on corpcard but a separate "incidentals" folio ($45 EUR) hit my personal card because the front desk wouldn't accept the corpcard for incidentals. They gave an itemized invoice. Should I submit the incidentals as reimbursement and will VAT be treated differently?

Tom (Finance): Thanks for flagging. Submit as reimbursement for the incidentals line item. For VAT: if the incidentals receipt shows VAT separately and you paid personally, we can only reclaim VAT if the merchant provides a valid VAT invoice in company name. Most hotels combine VAT on room; incidental VAT is often not reclaimable unless the vendor issues a business invoice. Finance will check the attached invoice.

Ellen: I attached: https://files.redwood.example/receipts/2004501234-hotel-itemized.pdf The incidentals line has VAT: 9%. The hotel invoice header is in my name, not company.

Priya (Ops): For reconciliation, include the room folio number and the hotel tax ID. If they can reissue an invoice to Redwood Inference for the incidentals we can do VAT reclaim. Otherwise it's reimbursable net of VAT rules.

Ellen: I asked the hotel to reissue an invoice to Redwood Inference; they said maybe in 2-3 days. I submitted expense EXP-4518, payment method = Personal Card, category = Travel - Accommodation Incidentals. Note: waiting on reissued invoice.

ExpenseBot: EXP-4518 received. Status: pending manager and finance review. ETA 3 business days.

Liam (Manager): I approve the reimbursement contingent on the reissued invoice if vendor can provide it. Approved for policy exception if they cannot reissue.

Tom (Finance): Reviewing. Two paths: 1) Vendor reissues invoice to company -> we process expense and attempt VAT reclaim. 2) Vendor cannot -> reimburse full amount but mark VAT not reclaimable (GL: Travel - Misc expenses; VAT flagged N/A). Please include the hotel's response when available.

Ellen: Hotel replied: they will reissue invoice to company but need a copy of our VAT number. Sent them Redwood VAT ID.

Priya (Ops): Nice. When the new invoice arrives, upload to the same expense EXP-4518 so we don't create duplicates. Travel ops will follow up with vendor if it's delayed.

Tom (Finance): Approved. If the vendor delays beyond 10 business days we will still process reimbursement and then handle VAT reclaim later if invoice arrives.

ExpenseBot: EXP-4518 status updated: Approved by manager and finance pending supporting invoice.

Ellen: Invoice received and uploaded. Thanks everyone.

Tom (Finance): Final note: reimbursement method = bank transfer (as selected). Expect payment after standard processing window. Closing thread.
